voices.note: the Gemara's own voice of this piska: the hekesh and narrative of 16a.20, the wording questions, the מאי טעמא answers, the ותניא/דתניא proofs and the reckoning of 17a
Ahasuerus, whose words (ווי מביתא ווי מברא) R' Elazar reports at 16a.21
ואמרי לה (16a.23): the second account of the two subsidings
Joseph the patriarch, whose words R' Elazar reports (16b.3, 16b.7)
ותניא (16b.9): R' Eliezer the Great on Deut 28:10
רבי שילא איש כפר תמרתא, whose derasha R' Chanina bar Pappa reports (דרש, 16b.11)
Queen Esther, whose words R' Yochanan reports (16b.14)
ואמרי לה אמר רבי אסי (16b.15) -- the variant attribution of the scoring dictum
ואיתימא רב שמואל בר מרתא (16b.19) -- the variant attribution
דאמר מר (16b.20-17a.1): why were Ishmael's years counted
ותניא (17a.2): Jacob 63 at his blessing; Ishmael died then
דתניא (17a.5): Jacob hidden fourteen years in Ever's house
דתניא (17a.6): Joseph away twenty-two years, as Jacob was
דתניא (17a.7): eighteen months in Sukkot, six in Beit El
Jacob the patriarch, speaker of Gen 47:9 (130 years)

props.gloss_en: for he went and found ministering angels in the likeness of men uprooting the trees of the garden; he asked what they were doing, and they said: Haman commanded us
the verse: 'and Haman was falling upon the couch' (Esth 7:8) -- quoted as the object of the stam's difficulty
R' Elazar: [the present tense 'falling'] teaches that an angel came and pushed him onto it
[Ahasuerus] said: woe in the house and woe outside -- 'will he even force the queen before me in the house?'
R' Elazar: Charbona too was wicked and in that plot; once he saw his plot would not succeed, he fled at once
and this is what is written: 'it hurls at him and does not spare; he would flee from its hand' (Job 27:22)
the verse: 'and the king's wrath subsided' (Esth 7:10) -- the doubled form the stam asks about
one subsiding was of the King of the world, and one of Ahasuerus
and some say: one [subsiding of wrath] over Esther and one over Vashti
the verse: 'to each of them he gave changes of clothing, and to Benjamin he gave five changes' (Gen 45:22)
Rav: because of two sela's weight of fine wool that Jacob gave Joseph beyond his brothers, the matter rolled on and our fathers went down to Egypt
R' Binyamin bar Yefet: [the five changes] hinted to him that a descendant would issue from him who would go out from before the king in five royal garments
as it is said: 'and Mordechai went out from before the king in royal apparel of blue...' (Esth 8:15)
the verse: 'and he fell upon the necks [plural] of Benjamin his brother' (Gen 45:14)
R' Elazar: [Joseph] wept over two Temples destined to be in Benjamin's portion and destined to be destroyed
'and Benjamin wept upon his necks': he wept over the Tabernacle of Shiloh, destined to be in Joseph's portion and destined to be destroyed
Joseph: as I bear nothing in my heart against Benjamin my brother, who was not party to my sale, so I bear nothing against you
'that it is my mouth that speaks to you' (Gen 45:12): as my mouth, so is my heart
R' Elazar, answering the stam's מאי מטוב מצרים: 'of the good of Egypt' (Gen 45:23) is aged wine that he sent him
for the mind of the elderly is pleased by it
first placement: 'and his brothers also went and fell before him' (Gen 50:18) is what people say: the fox in its hour -- bow to it
relocated: the proverb was said of 'and Israel bowed upon the head of the bed' (Gen 47:31) -- the fox in its hour, bow to it
'and he comforted them and spoke to their hearts' (Gen 50:21) teaches that he told them words the heart accepts
Joseph: if ten lamps could not put out one lamp, how can one lamp put out ten?
'light' (Esth 8:16) -- this is Torah
and so it says: 'for the commandment is a lamp and Torah is light' (Prov 6:23)
'gladness' -- this is the festival
and so it says: 'and you shall be glad on your festival' (Deut 16:14)
'joy' -- this is circumcision
and so it says: 'I rejoice over Your word' (Ps 119:162)
'and honour' -- these are tefillin
and so it says: 'and all the peoples of the earth shall see that the name of the Lord is called upon you, and they shall fear you' (Deut 28:10)
R' Eliezer the Great: [the name of the Lord called upon you, Deut 28:10] -- these are the head-tefillin
Rav Adda of Jaffa: the ten sons of Haman and [the word] 'ten' must be said in one breath
what is the reason? their souls all departed together
R' Yochanan: the vav of 'Vayzata' must be drawn out like a pole, like the steering-oar of Liburnian ships
what is the reason? they were all hanged on one pole
R' Sheila: all the songs are written half-brick over whole brick and whole brick over half-brick
except this song [the list of Haman's sons], written half-brick over half-brick and whole brick over whole brick
and [the list of] the kings of Canaan, written the same way
what is the reason? that their downfall have no rising
R' Abbahu: [Esth 9:12] teaches that an angel came and slapped him on his mouth
the verse: 'and when she came before the king, he said with the letter' (Esth 9:25)
R' Yochanan: the 'said' is Esther's -- she said to him 'let it be said'
Esther: let what is written in the letter be said by mouth
R' Tanchum: [the Megilla] requires scoring, like the truth of the Torah
the scoring requirement is learned from 'words of peace and truth' (Esth 9:30)
the verse: 'and the decree of Esther confirmed [these matters of Purim]' (Esth 9:32)
R' Yochanan: 'the matters of the fasts and their cry' and 'the decree of Esther confirmed these matters of Purim' (Esth 9:31-32) are read together
'to most of his brethren' (Esth 10:3), not to all: this teaches that some of the Sanhedrin parted from him
Rav Yosef: Torah study is greater than saving lives
for at first Mordechai is counted after four, and in the end after five
at first it is written (Ezra 2:2) ... Seraiah, Reelaiah, Mordechai; and in the end it is written (Neh 7:7) ... Azariah, Raamiah, Nahamani, Mordechai
Rav: Torah study is greater than building the Temple
for as long as Baruch ben Neriah lived, Ezra did not leave him to go up
Rav Yitzchak bar Shmuel bar Marta: Torah study is greater than honouring father and mother
for all those years our father Jacob was in Ever's house, he was not punished
Mar: why were Ishmael's years counted? to reckon Jacob's years by them -- 'and these are the years of the life of Ishmael, 137 years' (Gen 25:17)
how much older was Ishmael than Isaac? fourteen years (Gen 16:16, 21:5); how old was Ishmael when Jacob was born? seventy-four (Gen 25:26)
how many of his years remained? sixty-three -- so Jacob was sixty-three when Ishmael died
the baraita: Jacob was sixty-three when he was blessed by his father, and at that time Ishmael died
the baraita: from 'daughter of Ishmael' do I not know she was Nebaioth's sister? [it is said] to teach that Ishmael betrothed her and died, and Nebaioth her brother married her off (Gen 28:9)

(entertained) sixty-three and fourteen until Joseph is born make seventy-seven; Joseph thirty before Pharaoh (Gen 41:46) makes 107; seven of plenty and two of famine make 116 -- Jacob's age on reaching Egypt
Jacob to Pharaoh: 'the days of the years of my sojournings are 130 years' (Gen 47:9) -- against the 116 of the reckoning
rather, learn from it: the fourteen years he was in Ever's house are not counted [in the reckoning]
the baraita: Jacob was hidden in Ever's house fourteen years ... so when he stood at the well he was seventy-seven
the baraita: Joseph was away from his father twenty-two years, just as Jacob our father was away from his
rather: the fourteen he was in Ever's house are not counted [in the measure of his punishment]
rather, because he tarried two years on the road
the baraita: he left Aram Naharaim and came to Sukkot and spent eighteen months there
as it is said: 'and Jacob journeyed to Sukkot and built himself a house, and made booths for his cattle' (Gen 33:17)
and in Beit El he spent six months and offered sacrifices

schemas.gloss_en: והמלך קם בחמתו ... והמלך שב מגנת הביתן (Esth 7:7-8): מקיש שיבה לקימה -- מה קימה בחימה, אף שיבה בחימה
ומה עשרה נרות לא יכלו לכבות נר אחד, נר אחד היאך יכול לכבות עשרה נרות? -- ten against one, the easier extinguishing, failed; one against ten surely fails (= p_asara_nerot)

supports.gloss_en: ותניא, רבי אליעזר הגדול אומר: אלו תפילין שבראש -- the verse Rav Yehuda adduces is read of tefillin
ותניא: היה יעקב אבינו בשעה שנתברך מאביו בן ששים ושלש שנה, ובו בפרק מת ישמעאל
דתניא: היה יעקב בבית עבר מוטמן ארבע עשרה שנה
ומנלן דלא איענש? דתניא: נמצא יוסף שפירש מאביו עשרים ושתים שנה כשם שפירש יעקב -- the measure for measure counts only twenty-two
דתניא: ... ועשה שם שמונה עשר חדש ... ובבית אל עשה ששה חדשים -- two years on the road

challenges.gloss_en: תעלא? מאי בצירותיה מאחוה? -- a fox?! was Joseph lesser than his brothers? (answered by relocating the dictum: אלא אי איתמר הכי איתמר)

objections.gloss_en: נופל -- נפל מיבעי ליה! the verse should have said 'fell', not 'falling'

answered_by.gloss_en: מלמד שבא מלאך והפילו עליה (= p_malach_hipilo)

objections.gloss_en: שתי שכיכות הללו למה? why a doubled subsiding?

answered_by.gloss_en: אחת של מלכו של עולם ואחת של אחשורוש (= p_shechicha_hkbh)
ואמרי לה: אחת של אסתר ואחת של ושתי (= p_shechicha_esther_vashti)

objections.gloss_en: אפשר דבר שנצטער בו אותו צדיק יכשל בו? -- as Rav said, for two sela of wool our fathers went down to Egypt; could Joseph favour Benjamin in the same way?

answered_by.gloss_en: רמז רמז לו -- a hint of Mordechai's five royal garments (= p_remez_mordechai)

objections.gloss_en: כמה צוארין הוו ליה לבנימין? -- how many necks had Benjamin?
אמר -- אמרה מיבעי ליה! it was Esther who came, so the verse should say 'she said'

answered_by.gloss_en: אמרה לו: יאמר בפה מה שכתוב בספר (= p_amar_esther, p_yeamer_bapeh)

objections.gloss_en: מאמר אסתר -- אין, דברי הצומות -- לא?! did not the fasts too establish Purim?

answered_by.gloss_en: דברי הצומות ... ומאמר אסתר קיים -- read the two verses together (= p_kra_echad)

objections.gloss_en: דיעקב תלתין ושיתא הויין! -- Jacob was away thirty-six years, not twenty-two

answered_by.gloss_en: אלא: ארביסר דהוה בבית עבר לא חשיב להו (= p_arbesar_lo_leonesh)

objections.gloss_en: סוף סוף דבית לבן עשרין שנין הויין! -- even without Ever's house, Laban's was only twenty

answered_by.gloss_en: אלא משום דאשתהי באורחא תרתין שנין (= p_ishtahi_beorcha)
